findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — permDenialCache entries are never invalidated when permissions/roles change: the key embeds the resource name and parent folder, so the existing per-user/per-action invalidation (which can only Delete an exact key) cannot remove denial entries, leaving a user who is granted access denied for up to shortCacheTTL even if permCache is invalidated/refreshed.
[Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — the denial entry is written after the DB read, so a permission grant that races the write gets persisted as a denial.

[Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey omits the identity type: Check writes denial entries for all identity types (including anonymous and render service, whose UserUID is empty) and the lookup happens before type dispatch, so denials with an empty UID collide across identity types (e.g., a denial cached for a render-service check will deny anonymous users, or vice versa, for the same action/name/parent); this is also asymmetric since render-service positive results are deliberately never cached while its denials are.

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:~975 ('Should deny on explicit cache deny entry') — the test is vacuous: it sets the cached permission to a deny value while the comment claims 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked', so the test passes even if permDenialCache is never consulted and the denial-cache short-circuit (the core new behavior) is not actually verified; the cached perm should be set to true.

[Low/data] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-140 — permissionCacheUsage semantics are now misleading: a denial-cache hit is counted as a permission-cache hit ('true') and a perm-cache hit whose permissions are insufficient is counted as a miss ('false') before falling through to the DB, so the metric no longer reflects the actual permCache hit rate, breaking dashboards/alerts that consume it.

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey shares the namespace + '.perm_' prefix with userPermCacheKey and both cacheWrap instances are backed by the same underlying cache store, so keys can collide across the two caches (e.g., a perm key for an action containing underscores vs. a denial key with split name/parent components), causing cross-cache type confusion on read; a distinct prefix such as '.perm_deny_' should be used.

[Low/test_gap] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions has no test coverage for the anonymous branch (anonymousPermCacheKey lookup) or the render-service bypass; the new TestService_CacheCheck/TestService_CacheList tests only exercise TypeUser, and the removed getUserPermissions cache-hit test was not replaced with equivalent coverage for these paths.

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — permDenialCache entries are never invalidated when permissions/roles change: the key embeds the resource name and parent folder, so the existing per-user/per-action invalidation (which can only Delete an exact key) cannot remove denial entries, leaving a user who is granted access denied for up to shortCacheTTL even if permCache is invalidated/refreshed.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new permDenialCache is consulted first and causes an immediate deny when a key exists (permDenialKey via userPermDenialCacheKey embeds namespace/userUID/action/name/parent). The cache is populated whenever a DB-backed check returns !allowed (s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true)). From the diff, there is no corresponding deletion/invalidation path for these denial entries, and because the denial check happens before any fresh permission lookup, a later permission grant could still be denied until the shortCacheTTL expires (even if permCache is refreshed). The finding’s broader claim about existing invalidation mechanisms isn’t shown here, but the core “stale deny can block newly granted access until TTL” behavior is directly evidenced by the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — the denial entry is written after the DB read, so a permission grant that races the write gets persisted as a denial.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, a per-resource denial is cached only after fetching permissions from the DB and evaluating `allowed` (i.e., `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`). There is no invalidation/versioning tied to permission updates in the diff, so if permissions are granted concurrently after the DB read but before `permDenialCache.Set`, the code can write a stale denial entry that will cause subsequent requests to be denied purely from `permDenialCache.Get` (early return) until TTL expiry. This is an authorization correctness issue introduced by the new negative-cache path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey omits the identity type: Check writes denial entries for all identity types (including anonymous and render service, whose UserUID is empty) and the lookup happens before type dispatch, so denials with an empty UID collide across identity types (e.g., a denial cached for a render-service check will deny anonymous users, or vice versa, for the same action/name/parent); this is also asymmetric since render-service positive results are deliberately never cached while its denials are.

adjudication.rationale: In service.go, Check() computes permDenialKey using userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, ...) and consults s.permDenialCache **before** any identity-type dispatch (it happens before getCachedIdentityPermissions’ switch). The denial key (added in cache.go) does not include IdentityType, and Check() also writes denial entries unconditionally for any request (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`). Therefore, denials can collide across identity types that share the same UserUID value (including possibly empty), causing one identity’s cached denial to deny another. Additionally, render-service positive results are explicitly never cached in getCachedIdentityPermissions (TypeRenderService returns ErrNotFound) while its denials would still be cached, making the behavior inconsistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-140 — permissionCacheUsage semantics are now misleading: a denial-cache hit is counted as a permission-cache hit ('true') and a perm-cache hit whose permissions are insufficient is counted as a miss ('false') before falling through to the DB, so the metric no longer reflects the actual permCache hit rate, breaking dashboards/alerts that consume it.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, a permDenialCache hit increments permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (service.go: added block before DB fetch), even though it is not a permCache hit. Also, when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cached perms but checkPermission determines they don’t allow the requested resource, the function falls through and later increments permissionCacheUsage with label "false" (the unconditional increment after the cached-perms block), despite a real permCache hit. This makes the metric no longer represent actual permCache hit rate as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey shares the namespace + '.perm_' prefix with userPermCacheKey and both cacheWrap instances are backed by the same underlying cache store, so keys can collide across the two caches (e.g., a perm key for an action containing underscores vs. a denial key with split name/parent components), causing cross-cache type confusion on read; a distinct prefix such as '.perm_deny_' should be used.

adjudication.rationale: In cache.go, userPermCacheKey and the newly added userPermDenialCacheKey both build keys into the same underlying cache using the same prefix `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_"` and then concatenate additional fields with `_` separators. Because the concatenation is not an injective encoding (fields are not escaped/length-delimited), distinct logical entries across `permCache` (map[string]bool) and `permDenialCache` (bool) can produce the same string key when any component contains underscores and/or empty strings, which can cause cross-cache type confusion and incorrect reads. Using a distinct prefix (e.g., `.perm_deny_`) would avoid collisions between the two caches’ key spaces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions has no test coverage for the anonymous branch (anonymousPermCacheKey lookup) or the render-service bypass; the new TestService_CacheCheck/TestService_CacheList tests only exercise TypeUser, and the removed getUserPermissions cache-hit test was not replaced with equivalent coverage for these paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new branching logic in `getCachedIdentityPermissions` for `types.TypeAnonymous` (lookup via `anonymousPermCacheKey` in `permCache`) and `types.TypeRenderService` (explicit `cache.ErrNotFound` bypass). The added tests `TestService_CacheCheck`/`TestService_CacheList` only populate `idCache`/`permCache` for a user subject and thus exercise the `TypeUser`/`TypeServiceAccount` path; there is no test that drives the anonymous cache-key branch or verifies the render-service bypass behavior. Additionally, the prior cache-hit coverage in `TestService_getUserPermissions` was removed and not replaced for these new cached paths.
